Bottom line: the claim does not hold as stated. Its two cited evidence items (peak read-QPS, next-tier instance cost) cannot establish either half of the claim — they don't show the DB is actually read-bound rather than write/lock/vacuum/connection-bound (verified against PostgreSQL's own documentation), and they don't show p95 is dominated by query time or that a cold Redis cache will reach a useful hit rate in time. Given the asymmetric reversibility (cheap to reverse now, expensive once procurement lapses), a weighted trade-off robustly favors a third option over the binary (a)/(b) framing: proceed with the Postgres upgrade now and ship the Redis cache in parallel as independent, fully-scoped work, revisiting any future deferral only once real telemetry exists. Overall confidence: MEDIUM, capped by three unverified inputs (actual DB bottleneck type, actual procurement terms, and the trade-off's risk-tolerance weighting) that a reader can verify directly.
